key_idea: After Monty opens e empty doors, each of your doors still has probability 1/d while each other closed door has (d-s)/(d(d-s-e)) > 1/d, so switch to as many unselected doors as possible.
sketch: The initial pick is irrelevant by symmetry. Your s doors keep total mass s/d; the remaining mass (d-s)/d is spread evenly over the o = d-s-e unopened unselected doors, each strictly better than one of yours. Take k = min(s, o) of those and keep s-k of your own: answer k(d-s)/(d*o) + (s-k)/d. O(1) with doubles; pitfall is the case s > o where you cannot switch everything.
